prompt: Two parallel steel beams are crossed by a single diagonal brace, which acts as a transversal. One of the angles the brace makes with the upper beam measures $72^\circ$. What is the measure, in degrees, of the corresponding angle at the lower beam?
hint: Corresponding angles sit in matching positions at the two crossings — same corner, one beam down.

hints.text: Corresponding angles sit in matching positions at the two crossings — same corner, one beam down.
When the lines are parallel, corresponding angles are congruent.

explanation: Corresponding angles occupy the same relative position at each crossing (for example, upper-right at both).
When the two lines are parallel, corresponding angles are congruent.
So the matching angle at the lower beam is $72^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Slide the crossing down
steps: Imagine sliding the upper crossing straight down the brace until it lands on the lower beam.
Because the beams are parallel, the picture lands on itself perfectly — so the matching angle has to be the same $72^\circ$.
